sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Harsh Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
91 of 2023 at Police Station-Radha Nagar, District-Fatehpur under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The applicant is in jail since 05.05.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 21.09.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Harsh Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
Ravindra Pal vs State Of U.P. on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81367940/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. The applicant did not torture the deceased or demand dowry.
3. The deceased was a chronic patient of depression.
Her condition got aggravated despite regular medical attentions.
4. On the fateful day, the deceased succumbed to depression and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide.
5. The postmortem report opines the cause of death as asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

6. Injuries depicted in the postmortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i) Nature of ligature mark.
(ii).
The hyoid bone was intact.
7. The applicant did not aid or abet the suicide.
8. Prosecution evidence do not connect the applicant with the offence.
9. The prerequisite for attracting the presumption and the reversing the burden of proof are not established in the facts and circumstances and evidence of the case.
10. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
11. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of their influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Ravindra Pal be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 16.10.2023 Jaswant  Ravindra Pal vs State Of U.P. on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81367940/
